Question: How does the app work?
Answer: Residual capacity is calculated from the battery charge counter when charging reaches 100% with the "Charged" status (averaged across recent charges). Data is read via official Android BatteryManager APIs and supported kernel power_supply interfaces without requiring root access. Overall accuracy depends on the device fuel gauge and firmware.

Question: What is considered to be "Capacity Added"?
Answer: "Capacity Added" is the difference between the current capacity and the capacity recorded right before you connected the charger.

Question: Why does my battery show ~7.2V–8.9V, and why is the lightning icon green during fast charging?
Answer: Devices with Dual-Cell (2S series) batteries report total pack voltage around 7.2V–9.0V, which the app detects automatically (≥ 6000 mV = Dual-Cell) and normalizes per cell (3.60V–4.48V per cell during fast charging) before evaluating battery health status.

Question: How does "Idle Drain" calculate standby usage?
Answer: Idle Drain tracks battery percentage drop, estimated mAh consumed, and Deep Sleep vs. Awake time while the screen is off after unplugging the charger. For an accurate reading, leave the device idle on battery with the screen off for several minutes. Use the "Battery Usage" button to open Android's per-app power list if drain is high.

Question: What is the "Stress & Impedance" tab and the "Pulse Test (2s)"?
Answer: This lab estimates C-Rate load, Voltage Sag, internal resistance (Rint per cell), and a 3-vector electrochemical Stress Score (Thermal, Cathode Voltage, and Current). Tap "Pulse Test (2s)" while unplugged to apply a brief controlled CPU load and calibrate Rint directly from ΔV/ΔI.

Question: Where does the application get the "Charging Current Limit"?
Answer: The application reads "Charging Current Limit" from the kernel node "constant_charge_current_max" under /sys/class/power_supply/battery.

Question: Why is "Charging Current Limit" not displayed?
Answer: Not all kernels expose or allow read access to "constant_charge_current_max". When restricted or absent, this field is hidden.

Question: I have everything (or almost everything) in zeros. Why?
Answer: Some manufacturers omit or restrict fuel-gauge telemetry sensors, causing the Android API and kernel to report 0.

Question: Very large or small numbers appear for capacity, current, or voltage.
Answer: Open Settings, expand "More" inside the "Misc" section, and adjust the measurement units (μA/mA, μAh/mAh, mV/V) or enable Wh/Watt display.

Question: Available capacity stopped showing or appears intermittently.
Answer: This can indicate fuel-gauge instability, firmware bugs, or an aging battery controller.

Question: Residual capacity is higher than design capacity.
Answer: New batteries occasionally exceed nominal design capacity by a few percent. On older batteries, calibrate by discharging to 10% or lower and charging uninterrupted to 100% ("Charged"). Also verify that "Design Capacity" in Settings matches your device.

Question: Battery wear changes when the charger is disconnected.
Answer: When the charger is unplugged and current settles, the fuel gauge sometimes updates its reading slightly, resulting in a truer residual capacity measurement.

Question: Battery wear does not change even after months.
Answer: Wear only updates after qualifying calibration charges. Once every 1–2 months, discharge below 10% and charge fully to 100% until status shows "Charged" while the monitoring service is active.

Question: Battery wear fluctuates slightly with each charge.
Answer: This is normal due to temperature differences and ongoing chemical equilibrium inside lithium cells.

Question: Where does the app get "Number of Cycles (Android)"?
Answer: On Android 14+, the app first checks the system API (BatteryManager.EXTRA_CYCLE_COUNT), and falls back to supported kernel sysfs cycle nodes (such as /sys/class/power_supply/battery/cycle_count or bms/cycle_count).

Question: Why is "Number of Cycles (Android)" not displayed?
Answer: If neither the Android system API provides a positive cycle count nor any kernel cycle file is readable by normal apps, the field is omitted.
Tip #1: Avoid deep discharges below 10–15%. Frequent shallow cycles (roughly 20%–80%) keep cell degradation much lower.\n\n
Tip #2: Avoid extreme temperatures (below 0°C/32°F or above 40°C/104°F). High heat, especially combined with high charge voltage, rapidly accelerates cathode/SEI wear.\n\n
Tip #3: Do not leave the device plugged in at 100% for extended periods. Prolonged high voltage and repeated top-up micro-charges reduce cycle longevity.\n\n
Tip #4: Avoid heavy gaming or intensive workloads while fast charging. Combined Joule heating (I²R) and SoC heat significantly increase cell thermal stress.\n\n

Tip #5: Check \"Idle Drain\" and \"Stress & Impedance\" under Tools periodically. High standby drain (> 1.5%/h) points to background wakelocks, and keeping Stress Score in the optimal zone extends battery lifespan.

1. To calculate residual battery capacity and wear, keep the monitoring service enabled, discharge the battery to 10% or lower, and charge uninterrupted to 100% until status shows "Charged".
2. Continued charging briefly after reaching 100% is normal on modern devices (CV saturation phase).
3. Check that "Design Capacity" matches your battery specification under Settings → Misc → More.
4. If capacity, current, or voltage units look too large or small, adjust them in Settings → Misc → More. Devices with Dual-Cell (2S) batteries (~7.2V–9.0V) are detected automatically.
5. Use the Tools tab to monitor Idle Drain (screen-off standby drain & Deep Sleep) and Stress & Impedance (unplug charger before running the 2s Pulse Test calibration).
